17592186059580.question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_2 := R_2 +(- 4) \cdot R_1$ on $A?$
17592186059580.question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_2:=R_2 + (-4) R_1$ means that we need to add $-4$ times the first row to the second row. 

Carrying out this row operation, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4+(-4)(1) & 2+(-4)(2) & -1+(-4)(3) \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -13 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

17592186265809.question/problem:
Consider the matrix $C,$ given by

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $C?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
17592186265809.question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the second row to the first row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$

$$

	x_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} (3 + 1) = 2.
